subject: Discrepancy on May marketplace invoice - duplicate metering lines & VAT routing
messages:
From: BrightLane AP <accounts-payable@brightlane.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discrepancy on May invoice - duplicate marketplace lines (AWS + GCP)

Hi Jasmine,

We're reviewing our May charges and flagged a set of duplicate marketplace line items that appear to have been billed through both AWS Marketplace and GCP Marketplace for the same usage window and meter IDs. Attached: BrightLane_Invoice_May2026.pdf and a raw metering_export_may.csv from our billing system with the offending meter IDs highlighted.

Key example: Meter ID 3837-ALPHA appears on both the AWS line (line 42) and the GCP line (line 129) with identical usage units and timestamp ranges. Total potential overcharge ≈ $7,120.

We need:
- Confirmation that these are duplicates and not distinct entity-level charges
- Proposed remediation: credit memo or offset path (which marketplace will issue the credit)
- VAT handling: We're a UK entity and need to confirm if VAT was applied on both legs — we cannot accept duplicate VAT.

Please advise next steps and an ETA for remediation; our finance close for May is next Wednesday (2026-05-26).

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Accounts Payable / BrightLane AI
attachments: BrightLane_Invoice_May2026.pdf, metering_export_may.csv

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@brightlane.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-05-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on May invoice - duplicate marketplace lines (AWS + GCP)

Hi Marta — thanks for the detail and the CSV, that helps.

I'm looping in Marissa from Finance to validate the ledger and Karthik from Sales so we can coordinate the marketplace-side credits. Ben (who manages partner billing) is on the thread for any marketplace seller reach-out.

Immediate plan:
- Finance (Marissa) to pull server-side metering and compare seller-provided line items to your CSV
- Sales/Partner (Karthik/Ben) to confirm which marketplace(s) actually issued the invoice and whether there's an internal reroute causing dual billings
- We'll prepare a reconciliation workbook and a proposed credit path (AWS offset vs GCP refund).

Can you confirm the BrightLane AWS Seller ID (if you have it) and whether you submitted usage through a reseller flow? That will determine whether AWS or GCP is the right channel for a refund.

I'll aim to get an initial reconciliation back by EOD Tuesday (2026-05-19).

— Jasmine
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>, Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@brightlane.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com, ben_carter@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-05-19T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on May invoice - duplicate marketplace lines (AWS + GCP)

Hi all — I pulled the marketplace settlement feeds and matched them against BrightLane's CSV. Preliminary findings (attached recon_workbook_may_2026.xlsx):

- Meter ID 3837-ALPHA: identical usage and timestamps appear in both AWS (settlement record AWR-2026-05-05-3837) and GCP (invoice GCP-INV-7653) feeds.
- Internal routing note: BrightLane was onboarded as a cross-cloud listing in late April; during the onboarding the usage router duplicated a subset of usage when a legacy reseller tag was present.
- Gross duplicate amount: $7,120. VAT shown on both lines for UK entity (20%) leading to a duplicate VAT exposure ≈ $1,424.

Recommendation:
1) Issue customer-facing credit of $7,120 plus a VAT credit memo of $1,424.
2) Route the gross credit via AWS Marketplace offset where possible for the AWS-billed lines (faster settlement), and request a refund request to Google for the GCP line (GCP refunds take longer).
3) Tax to confirm VAT reclassification for UK: should be reversed on the duplicate leg and a single VAT line remain on the corrected invoice. I've flagged this to Ben for KYC/seller ID confirmation.

I'll attach a cleaned CSV and workbook sections: ledger_match, seller_settlement_snapshots. ETA: I'll circulate the credit memo draft and suggested accounting entries by EOD 2026-05-19.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
attachments: recon_workbook_may_2026.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com, Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@brightlane.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-05-20T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on May invoice - duplicate marketplace lines (AWS + GCP)

Thanks Marissa — good catch. Quick notes from a marketplace/seller perspective:

- BrightLane's AWS Seller ID (from our onboarding record) is BLN-SLR-9923. Ben, please confirm if the onboarding reseller tag was used for both marketplaces (that would explain duplicate ingestion).
- Proposed operational path: open an AWS offset request referencing AWR-2026-05-05-3837 and submit a parallel refund request to Google (GCP ticket attached in our internal tracker).
- Timelines: AWS offsets are typically processed within one settlement cycle (30–45 days). GCP refunds historically take 45–90 days.

Action items:
- Ben to confirm reseller flag and provide seller console screenshots to Marta (Ben: please attach seller_account_screenshots.zip if available).
- Finance (Marissa) to draft the customer credit memo and VAT reversal line items.
- Jasmine to confirm with Marta whether BrightLane prefers a single consolidated credit via AWS (if we can re-route the GCP line) or split credits for audit purposes.

I'll assemble the mutual action plan and upload to the HubSpot ticket (link: https://app.hubspot.com/tickets/874321/BB-4892) with the expected milestones.

— Karthik
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Marta Ruiz <accounts-payable@brightlane.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-05-20T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on May invoice - duplicate marketplace lines (AWS + GCP)

Thanks — that path works for us. We prefer a single consolidated credit memo if possible (easier for our audit), but we're OK with split credits if marketplace rules require it.

I've uploaded a signed mutual action plan (signed_mutual_action_plan.pdf) authorizing Redwood to coordinate on our behalf with AWS and GCP for the May billing window and to accept offset credits against future invoices. Please proceed.

Requested next steps for Redwood:
- Share the draft customer credit memo and VAT reversal by EOD 2026-05-21
- Confirm expected timing for the AWS offset (best estimate) and initiation of GCP refund
- Provide a short note we can attach to our GL to explain the credit for our auditors (one paragraph with references to settlement IDs).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Accounts Payable / BrightLane AI
attachments: signed_mutual_action_plan.pdf
